REDEEM SKILLS RECRUITMENT SOLUTIONS (RECRUITER) on behalf of OneCare Priority Services Pty Ltd T/A OneCare Priority Services

Role: Care Supervisor 
Employer: OneCare Priority Services Pty Ltd T/A One Care Priority Services
Location: Campbelltown, South Australia 5074
Employment Type: Full-time, Permanent
Salary: AUD $72,000 – $82,000 per annum plus superannuation

ABOUT US

One Care Priority Services is a South Australia-based disability support provider located at 567 Lower North East Road, Campbelltown SA 5074, committed to delivering high-quality, person-centred services to individuals living with disabilities, injuries, and mental health conditions. The organisation operates across Adelaide and surrounding regions, supporting participants under the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS).

The company is focused on enhancing the quality of life of its clients by providing tailored support services that promote independence, dignity, and active participation in the community. All services are delivered in accordance with NDIS Practice Standards, relevant legislation, and organisational policies.

Position Overview:

We are seeking a compassionate and experienced Care Supervisor to lead our direct care team across aged care and disability support services. This is a full-time, ongoing supervisory role shall be responsible for overseeing the planning, coordination and delivery of high-quality, person-centred care services to older people and individuals with complex support needs and to supervise, guide and support a team of aged care workers, disability support workers and personal care workers, while ensuring all services are delivered in compliance with legislative, ethical and quality standards.

Key Duties and Responsibilities:

Service Coordination & Delivery

•	Coordinate, monitor and review individualised care and support services for older people and NDIS participants, ensuring services are responsive to changing client needs and aligned with their goals
•	Facilitate the development, implementation and ongoing review of individual service plans in collaboration with clients, families and multidisciplinary teams
•	Coordinate client-directed services, supporting consumer choice and control in all aspects of service delivery
•	Deliver and oversee care services using a palliative approach, providing dignified end-of-life care in accordance with best practice standards

Supervision & Workforce Leadership

•	Supervise aged care workers, disability support workers and personal care workers on a day-to-day basis, providing clear direction, mentoring and performance guidance
•	Conduct regular team briefings, support debriefs and individual supervision sessions to maintain workforce wellbeing and service quality
•	Identify training and development needs within the team and provide or coordinate relevant training, coaching and support
•	Promote independence and community participation among staff and clients alike

Risk Management & Complex Needs

•	Identify, assess and implement targeted interventions for older people at risk, including those experiencing social isolation, functional decline or complex health presentations
•	Escalate concerns appropriately and contribute to risk management planning in line with organisational policy and legislative obligations

Compliance & Governance

•	Manage legal and ethical compliance across all service activities, including adherence to the Aged Care Quality Standards, NDIS Practice Standards and relevant South Australian legislation
•	Maintain accurate client records, incident reports and service documentation in accordance with privacy and confidentiality obligations
•	Ensure all staff operate within their scope of practice and comply with relevant certifications and compliance requirements (Police Check, NDIS Worker Screening, etc.)

Partnerships & Networks

•	Develop and maintain professional networks and collaborative partnerships with health services, community organisations, allied health professionals and government agencies
•	Manage and review partnership agreements with contracted service providers, ensuring obligations are met and service quality is upheld
•	Represent One Care in stakeholder meetings, case conferences and community forums as required

TO BE SUCCESSFUL IN THIS ROLE YOU WILL REQUIRE:

•	AQF Certificate IV in Individual support or higher relevant qualification is required.
•	12 months full-time or equivalent part-time or casual basis employment with proven experience is required in relevant field. 
•	Demonstrated experience supervising or leading a team in a care setting is highly desirable
•	Valid Australian driver’s license is must, along with comprehensive car insurance. 
•	Applicants must be willing to accept shift allocations at client locations across metropolitan, regional, and outer regional South Australia, depending on operational requirements and client care needs. Flexibility to travel between client locations is an essential requirement of this position.
•	Strong interpersonal skills, a compassionate, patient approach.
•	Ability to work independently and as part of team.
•	A valid National Police Check, Working with Children Check and other NDIS entry level certificates are required.
•	First Aid, Manual Handling and CPR Certificate is required.
•	Sound understanding of the aged care and/or NDIS legislative frameworks
Additional Requirements:
•	Willingness to undertake ongoing training including WHS, infection control, and medication administration

BENEFITS

•	Work in a supportive and inclusive team environment.
•	Opportunities for career development and training.
•	Flexible working arrangements to suit your lifestyle.
•	Meaningful work where you make a real impact.
•	Opportunity to make a real difference in the lives of others

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Your role at St John of God Accord

We are currently seeking enthusiastic and motivated Community Support Workers to provide high-quality support to individuals attending our Day Services and Group Programs across our Community Campuses in Melbourne's north and west, including Greensborough, Glenroy and Sydenham.

As a Community Support Worker, you will work a variety of shifts between 8:30am and 4:30pm, Monday to Friday.

Positions are offered on a casual basis, with the potential for permanent employment for the right candidates.

The Position

Participate in a range of appropriate programs and activities (recreational, pre-vocational, education and social) aimed at increasing the individual's skills and access to and participation in the community

Provide the highest level of support for all individuals supported and ensure each person supported is treated with respect that enhances their personal worth, dignity and rights, at all times

Assist in achieving individual's, team and service goals and objectives.

Seek ways of improving the standards of service by working closely with colleagues, relevant line managers and contributing to meetings

Maintain a high level of service for all individual's and ensure the health, wellbeing and safety of all people supported and staff is maintained at all times

Support the identified needs of individuals in relation to their particular life circumstances

Ensure that where required attendance to personal care needs of clients is undertaken in a professional, empathetic and timely manner

You will have experience liaising with families and circles of support, service providers and community groups, sound written & communication skills, able to multi-task and work under pressure and capable of working independently with an individual or group of people.

Successful applicants must be eligible for a NDIS screening check, hold a valid Australian Drivers Licence, Working with Children check and First Aid Level 2 certificate. 

Experience in the disability sector and-or possession of a relevant qualification will be highly regarded.

Above all, patient care will be at the core of everything you do committing to and supporting our Mission and Values.

We can offer:

Hourly rate: $32.87 to $51.81 (inclusive of causal loading) plus 12% Superannuation

Casual positions available

We offer a range of salary packaging options tailored to your employment status such as mortgage, rent, meal entertainment, holiday accommodation or other everyday living expenses - up to $18,550 as a permanent employee and a percentage of your earnings as a casual

A healthy work-life balance through flexible work options & well-being programs

Employee discount on St John of God Hospital & Medical Services and Private Health Insurance

St John of God Accord (SJGA) complies with the NDIS Commission and all prospective employees are required to apply for your NDIS Check to ensure the safety and wellbeing of people with a disability.

For enquiries contact Steven Williams, Manager Community Campuses and Employment Services on (03) 8468 1156.

Please note: If suitable candidates are identified, shortlisting and interviews may begin before the advertisement closes.

Job Summary: Lead our SEO & Google Ads team as Head of Digital Marketing with Localsearch  - shape strategy, drive results, and leave your mark on the Gold Coast.

Key Selling Points: 
•	Lead a talented team of SEO & Google Ads strategists in Robina 
•	Report directly to the CEO and shape company-wide strategy 
•	A senior, hands-on leadership role for strategy, people and performance lovers 

Who are we?
At Localsearch, we've been empowering Australian businesses with top-tier digital marketing solutions since 1993. Today, we stand as one of the largest digital marketing powerhouses in Australia, helping over 300,000 businesses grow online. Based in the heart of Robina, just steps from Robina Town Centre, our modern office is equipped with everything you need to thrive - including an on-site café with barista-made coffee, high-tech tools, and a collaborative, fun culture where your skills will shine!

What will you do?
As Head of Digital Marketing, you'll take ownership of Localsearch's SEO and paid search strategy, leading a team of Digital Strategists while reporting directly to our CEO. This is a senior, hands-on leadership role for someone who thrives on strategy, people and performance.
•	Develop and implement digital marketing strategies for SEO and paid search, with clearly defined plans and measurable goals
•	Conduct market research and analysis of search behaviour, competitor positioning, and channel trends to inform strategy
•	Advise the CEO on marketing investment priorities, channel mix, and emerging digital opportunities
•	Lead and develop a team of SEO and Google Ads Digital Strategists, setting clear performance expectations
•	Conduct regular one-on-ones and performance reviews to grow individual and team capability
•	Design and oversee digital marketing campaigns across SEO and Google Ads, grounded in audience insight and defined conversion objectives
•	Review and approve campaign strategies to ensure best-practice standards and deliverables are met
•	Oversee the SEO service offering across technical, on-page, content, and link building disciplines
•	Analyse marketing performance across channels, interpreting results against KPIs and presenting recommendations to the CEO
•	Monitor market trends and benchmark performance against industry standards to drive continuous improvement

Who are you & what will you bring?
We're after an experienced digital marketing leader who combines specialist SEO and Google Ads expertise with strong people leadership and commercial acumen.
Required:
•	Bachelor's Degree in Marketing, Business, Communications, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience
•	Relevant senior experience in a specialist digital marketing role, with expertise in SEO and paid search, ideally in a digital agency or managed services environment
•	Experience leading and developing a team of digital marketing strategists
•	Experience planning and managing digital marketing campaigns across SEO and paid search for multi-client portfolios
•	Experience conducting market research and using consumer behaviour insights to shape marketing strategy
•	Experience at a senior level with direct engagement with executive leadership
•	Specialist knowledge of SEO and Google Ads
•	Strong leadership and people management skills, with the ability to coach and hold a team accountable
•	Strong marketing analytics capability, able to interpret data and translate insights into clear recommendations
•	Strong communication skills, able to present complex digital concepts clearly to stakeholders and clients
•	Highly organised with the ability to manage competing priorities without compromising quality

395 Collins Street Melbourne VIC 3000, Australia
Location
395 Collins Street , Melbourne VIC 3000
Pastry Cook – Full-Time (38 hours/week)
Position: Pastry Cook ( Level 3 ANZSCO - Cook grade 3 Level 4 Restaurant Award). 
Job Type: Full-Time (38 hours/week)
Business Name: Collins Coffee House 
Salary: $70,000 – $80,000 per annum (plus superannuation)
Location: 395 Collins Street , Melbourne VIC 3000
Start Date: December 2026 January 2027
About us
Located in the heart of Melbourne, 
Collins Coffee House was founded in December 2019 with a vision to source produce from local businesses and serve Melburnians their favourite coffee, cakes, and savoury delights baked by Laura the owner and head pastry chef.
Just months later, we faced the unexpected challenge of covid-19. As lockdowns emptied our city, we were forced to close our doors due to lockdowns and a city that had turned into a ghost town.
During this time, Laura found solace in baking for her family, sparking the idea for our “High Tea in a Box” originally created as a one-time Mother’s Day gift. With nothing more than a simple letterbox drop in the local area, the response was overwhelming. Orders poured in, and what started as a heartfelt gesture turned into a lifeline.
Through dedication, long hours, and unwavering community support, Collins Coffee House not only survived but flourished.
Today, we are proud to welcome guests into our historical building, serving what is now known as Melbourne’s Best High Tea. All thanks to the love and support of our incredible customers.
We are currently seeking a skilled and passionate full-time Pastry Cook to join our team.
About the Role
The Pastry Cook is responsible for preparing, baking, decorating, and presenting a variety of pastries, cakes, desserts, breads, and other baked goods in accordance with established recipes, quality standards, and food safety requirements. The role requires the application of specialised pastry-making techniques to produce high-quality products that meet customer expectations.
The Pastry Cook will work collaboratively with the kitchen team to ensure efficient production, maintain inventory levels, monitor product quality, and contribute to menu development. The position requires strong technical skills, attention to detail, creativity, and the ability to work effectively in a fast-paced commercial kitchen environment while maintaining high standards of hygiene and workplace safety.
Tasks/responsibilities:
- Preparing, baking, and decorating pastries, cakes, desserts, biscuits, breads, and other baked products.
- Measuring and combining ingredients according to recipes and production requirements.
- Preparing doughs, batters, fillings, creams, icings, and other pastry components.
- Monitoring baking times, temperatures, and product quality to ensure consistency and compliance with standards.
- Decorating and finishing pastry products to meet presentation and customer requirements.
- Developing and testing new pastry items and seasonal products.
- Ensuring all products are prepared and presented to a high standard of quality.
- Checking the quality of raw ingredients and finished products.
- Maintaining stock levels and assisting with ordering ingredients and supplies.
- Operating, cleaning, and maintaining baking and pastry equipment.
- Ensuring compliance with food safety, hygiene, and workplace health and safety requirements.
- Assisting with production planning, menu development, and cost control.
- Supervising and providing guidance to junior kitchen staff and apprentices as required.
Skills and Experience
AQF Certificate III in Patisserie, Certificate IV in Patisserie, or equivalent relevant qualification.
At least 3 year of relevant experience as a Pastry Cook or Baker in a commercial bakery, café, or kitchen environment.
Sound knowledge of pastry preparation, dough handling, baking techniques, and dessert production.
Ability to follow recipes and maintain consistency, quality, and presentation standards.
Understanding of food safety, hygiene, and workplace health and safety procedures.
Strong time management skills and ability to work efficiently during busy production periods.
Good attention to detail and ability to work both independently and collaboratively within a team environment.
Flexibility to work across weekdays, weekends, early mornings, and public holidays as required.
Why Join Us
Opportunity to contribute to the preparation of high-quality pastries and baked goods.
Supportive and friendly team environment.
Stable, full-time position in a popular destination bakery with strong community support.
Competitive salary package of $70,000 – $80,000 per year, commensurate with skills and experience.
How to Apply
